findings.title: Apache HTTPd 2.4.49 Path Traversal (CVE-2021-41773)
findings.description: A path traversal and remote code execution vulnerability exists in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49. An attacker can map URLs to files outside the directories configured by Alias-like directives.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution and arbitrary file read on the web server.
findings.remediation: Upgrade Apache HTTP Server to version 2.4.50 or later immediately. Apply vendor security patches.

findings.title: Weak TLS 1.0 Protocol Supported
findings.description: The server supports TLS 1.0, which is deprecated and vulnerable to BEAST and POODLE attacks.
findings.impact: An attacker in a privileged network position could decrypt TLS-protected traffic.
findings.remediation: Disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. Configure minimum TLS version to TLS 1.2. Prefer TLS 1.3.

findings.title: Missing HSTS Header
findings.description: The web server does not return a Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header, allowing downgrade attacks.
findings.impact: Users may be redirected to HTTP, exposing credentials to interception.
findings.remediation: Add header: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
